accuracy.evidence: Checked against NGSS 3-PS2-1 and its clarification statement (balanced forces pushing on a box from both sides produce no motion; unbalanced forces change motion), DfE KS3 physics (balanced forces, resultant force, newtons) and BBC Bitesize KS2/KS3 forces. The lab model is Newton's second law with a nominal mass: dots every 0.25 s are equally spaced when net force is 0 and spread when it is not; the rolling-trolley step clamps speed at 0 so friction never pushes it backwards; the tug step says the box is on wheels so ignoring friction is stated, not hidden. Numbers recomputed: 8 − 3 = 5 N left, 6 − 4 net for push 10 v friction 4; parameterised items checked at corners (p1 7..10 v 2..6, m2 6..10 v 1..5, all positive). Adult text now places 'balanced and unbalanced' at KS3 in England rather than claiming a Year 3 statement.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented forces misconceptions (Driver et al. 1994, Making Sense of Secondary Science, ch. 18; AAAS Project 2061 item bank on 'force needed to keep motion'): still objects have no forces (challenge 'none', m3), moving objects need an unbalanced force (prediction 3, challenge 'move', p3, m4), the 'stronger-looking' team wins regardless of size (prediction 1), the smaller force wins or nothing moves when both pull (prediction 2, 'small', 'still'), and an unfair test that changes two variables (fair-test feedback when the left pull changes, 'fair', 'count', m7).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbalf is an investigation lab: the learner sets two pulls, lets go and reads a dot trail as evidence, logs each trial in a results list, runs a one-variable fair test, keeps a rolling trolley steady against friction and pushes a puck from behind, in front and the side. flagfdiag draws scaled arrows on squared paper; flagdrop is about gravity and supports; flagfrict compares surfaces. Max 6-shingle similarity 3.8% (flag_bgraph.js); explanation overlap 0.9% (Drawing force diagrams).

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each rule before the text names it: the 6 N / 6 N trial leaves a single dot (no motion), the 8 N / 3 N trial sends the box left with growing gaps, the fair-test runs at right 6, 8, 10 N show gaps widening more each time, the trolley at push 4 N leaves evenly spaced dots while push 1 N leaves shrinking gaps, and the puck path bends only for the side push.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'moves to the team that looks stronger' (equal newtons give a single dot), 'right, towards the 3 N team' or 'nowhere, both teams pull' (the trail goes left), and for the rolling trolley 'slows down and stops' (even dot spacing at push = friction). A fair-test prediction also checks 'the same every time'.

challenge_feedback.evidence: slip() has 8 distinct messages (none, more, still, small, move, count, fair, dir), each naming the slip, e.g. 'If the table pushed 10 N up, the book would jump up. Balanced means equal: 5 N.' and 'More tests help, but the real problem is that two things changed at once.' In-lab feedback is specific too: changing the left pull in the fair test explains why it must stay at 5 N.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the family audience: kid FK 1.4, adult FK 8.8. Kid text uses push, pull, newtons, same size, opposite ways, faster and faster, with one worked case (6 N and 6 N). Canvas labels shrink to fit at 360 px.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases; explanation overlap under 1% with every lesson). Kid paragraphs: force and newtons with balanced example; unbalanced; balanced while moving; fair test. Adult paragraphs: standard and key words; definitions; named mistakes; what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots after Show me on every step at 360 px Android in light and dark, plus desktop light: the results list, arrow labels, dot trail and status line fit with no clipping; the puck zones carry text labels; control buttons wrap below the canvas and are at least 44 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag or tap has a button twin ('Left pull one newton more', 'Let go and watch the box', 'Push from the side'). The canvas aria-label and narration update after each action and each trial result. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors.
